text:
oliver: Quick copy check for the Dedicated pool deletion flow. Current modal says: "Delete pool? This action cannot be undone." with buttons "Cancel" / "Delete". Feels abrupt for a bill-impacting operation.

ria: Agree. We should surface billing and data retention implications up front. Also softening language helps ("remove" vs "delete").

harper: Proposal A (clear consequences):
Headline: "Remove reserved capacity"
Body: "Removing this pool will stop billing for reserved GPUs and deallocate instances. Logs and metrics will be retained for 30 days."
Primary CTA: "Remove pool"
Secondary CTA: "Cancel"

noah: Proposal B (safer):
Headline: "Deactivate pool temporarily"
Body: "You can pause this pool to stop new billing while keeping config and data. Use Delete to permanently remove it."
Primary CTA: "Pause pool"
Secondary CTA: "Delete permanently" (destructive, outlined red)

maya: Love the two-step idea. Product likes giving a safer default. If we add both options, confirm the UI won't overwhelm mobile. Buttons might need stacking.

oliver: UX constraint: modal height must remain < 420px. Keep copy tight. Also we must include a small line: "Your SLA will be paused while pool is deactivated." Is that OK to show here? Legal asked for simpler language.

ria: Wording suggestion to keep short: "Pausing stops billing and preserves pool config. Deleting removes config and stops retention." But that's a bit compressed. Maybe split into two bullets (short). Bullets are OK in modals.

harper: Accessibility / SR notes: include visually-hidden pool id and the exact effect line as aria-describedby. Use role=dialog and aria-modal=true. For the destructive CTA include aria-label: "Delete pool permanently. This action cannot be undone." so screen readers get the severity.

noah: Analytics: capture which CTA used (pause vs delete) and snapshot pool size to estimate cost impact. Also fire a confirm_delete_modal_shown event.

maya: Copy draft that balances clarity + brevity (hand-off):
Headline: "Pause or delete this reserved pool"
Body: "Pausing stops billing but keeps your configuration. Deleting permanently removes the pool and associated retention."
Bullets (condensed):
- "Pause: stop billing, keep settings"
- "Delete: permanently remove pool and data retention"
Primary (non-destructive) CTA: "Pause pool"
Primary aria-label: "Pause this reserved pool and stop billing"
Secondary (destructive) CTA: "Delete permanently"
Secondary aria-label: "Permanently delete this reserved pool. This cannot be undone."
Support note (small): "Need help? Contact Support to retain snapshots before deleting." (link)

ria: LGTM. Tiny language tweak: change "data retention" to "retained snapshots" if that's what we mean. More specific.

harper: Agree. Replace in body: "... and associated retained snapshots."

oliver: Finalized copy for PR (with aria notes) below. I'll update Figma and add tests for mobile stacking.

Final copy:
Headline: "Pause or delete this reserved pool"
Body: "Pausing stops billing but preserves your configuration. Deleting permanently removes the pool and any retained snapshots."
Bullets:
- "Pause: stop billing, keep settings"
- "Delete: permanently remove pool and retained snapshots"
Primary CTA: "Pause pool" (aria-label: "Pause this reserved pool and stop billing")
Secondary CTA: "Delete permanently" (aria-label: "Permanently delete this reserved pool. This cannot be undone.")
Support link: "Contact Support to retain snapshots" -> /support/retain-snapshots
ARIA: modal role=dialog, aria-modal=true, visually-hidden pool id included, destructive CTA flagged as aria-describedby to the warning text.

maya: Nice. I'll run a quick microtest with support and billing to confirm the 30-day language. If legal wants different phrasing we can swap retained snapshots -> logs.
